full.description: This is a low-power histological micrograph showing a cross-section of the gastrointestinal tract, specifically the duodenum. The tissue demonstrates chronic inflammation and structural disruption typical of a chronic peptic ulcer. Deep within the wall, there is extensive fibrosis and granulation tissue replacing normal layers. The findings are characteristic of a chronic peptic ulcer of the duodenum.

random.description: This image is a low-power photomicrograph of gastrointestinal tissue, likely showing the wall of the stomach or intestine. It demonstrates a large, well-circumscribed lesion or multiple nodular masses expanding the submucosa and muscular layers. The histological appearance is consistent with a gastrointestinal stromal tumor (GIST) or a similar mesenchymal neoplasm. The mucosa overlying the lesion appears partially compressed or unremarkable.
